question: Can the standard Gaussian diffusion model, with a space-time factorized 3D U-Net, generate temporally coherent video, including long and text-conditioned video?
hypothesis: Joint image-video training and a new reconstruction-guided conditional sampler improve video sample quality over plain training and replacement sampling.
contributions: Diffusion model for video using a 3D U-Net factorized over space and time, trainable jointly on images and video
Reconstruction-guided sampling for spatial and temporal extension, better than the replacement method
First results on large text-conditioned video generation; state of the art on UCF101 unconditional and BAIR/Kinetics-600 video prediction

method.summary: Standard continuous-time Gaussian diffusion with epsilon (or v) prediction and a 3D U-Net with 1x3x3 convs, spatial attention and added temporal attention blocks. Trained on fixed blocks of frames (16x64x64, 9x128x128); longer or higher-resolution video is made by reconstruction-guided conditional sampling from the unconditional model. Video prediction uses the unconditionally trained models.

datasets.name: UCF101
datasets.split: all 13,320 videos for training; 10,000 generated samples for FID/IS
datasets.source: Soomro et al. 2012 via TensorFlow Datasets
datasets.preprocessing: 16-frame segments at 64x64, TFDS loader without further processing

datasets.name: BAIR Robot Pushing
datasets.split: condition on 1 frame, generate next 15; eval set 256 examples

datasets.name: Kinetics-600
datasets.split: 50 thousand randomly sampled test videos; condition on 5 frames, generate next 11
datasets.source: Kay et al. 2017; Carreira et al. 2018

datasets.name: Text-video dataset
datasets.split: 4096 samples for metrics, scored against training and validation sets
datasets.preprocessing: captions as BERT-large embeddings with attention pooling

other.role_note: super-resolution plus autoregressive extension, conditioned on 16x64x64 frameskip-4 samples

training.objective: weighted MSE denoising loss; epsilon-prediction with t sampled by cosine schedule; v-prediction for BAIR and Kinetics

inference.decoding: ancestral sampler; predictor-corrector with Langevin step (delta=0.1)

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: C3D features on UCF101; Inception on text-to-video, avg over frames or first frame only

metrics.name: IS
metrics.definition: Inception score; C3D on UCF101, I3D on Kinetics; text-to-video two numbers from 1 and 10 splits

eval.protocol: Text-to-video FID and FVD given as two numbers (against training / validation sets). BAIR FVD: 100x256 samples vs 256 eval examples. Kinetics: samples without replacement, same subsequences for samples and ground truth. No seed counts stated.

limits: Text-video dataset (10 million captioned videos) is not named or described further; no release of models
Fixed small blocks (16 frames, 64x64 or 128x128); longer videos come from autoregressive extension
UCF101 evaluated at 64x64 which the authors say may disadvantage it versus higher-resolution works
Metric protocols vary across the literature so cross-paper scores differ slightly
Independent images for joint training are drawn from the same video dataset, larger image datasets left to future work
Societal harm concerns: authors withhold models; text-to-video inherits bias, not audited

terms.definition: conditional sampling that adjusts the denoising prediction by the gradient of the reconstruction error of the conditioning data

lineage.note: Standard diffusion formulation and ancestral sampler

lineage.work: Score-based generative modeling through SDEs (Song et al.)
Diffusion probabilistic modeling for video generation (Yang et al.)
